questions.question: In the year 1926, which of the following month had 5 Fridays?
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

A month has **5 Fridays** if it has enough days such that one of the Fridays falls within the first three days of a 31-day month, the first two days of a 30-day month, or on the first day of a 29-day month. Specifically, in a month with **31 days**, if it starts on a **Friday**, **Thursday**, or **Wednesday**, it will contain 5 Fridays.

__Calculation:__

First, we determine if **1926** is a leap year. Since 1926 is not divisible by 4, it is an **ordinary year** with 365 days.

Now, let us find the day of the week on **January 1, 1926** by calculating the number of odd days:

Odd days until the year 1600 = 0

Odd days from 1601 to 1900 = 1

Odd days from 1901 to 1925 (25 years):

Number of leap years in 25 years = 25 ÷ 4 = 6 leap years

Total odd days in 25 years = 25 (one for each year) + 6 (extra for leap years) = 31 days

31 days ≡ 3 odd days (since 31 ÷ 7 leaves a remainder of 3)

Total odd days until **December 31, 1925** = 1 + 3 = 4 odd days.

The 4th odd day corresponds to **Thursday**. Therefore, **January 1, 1926** was a **Friday**.

**January** has 31 days. Since it started on a Friday, the Fridays in **January 1926** were:

January 1, 8, 15, 22, and 29.

This gives a total of **5 Fridays**.

Checking the other options for confirmation:

__
 
• **February 1926**: As an ordinary year, February had 28 days. 28 ÷ 7 = 4 weeks exactly, so it had only 4 Fridays.
 
• **March 1926**: Starts on Monday (as February 28 was Sunday). A 31-day month starting on Monday has 4 Fridays (5th, 12th, 19th, 26th).
 
• **May 1926**: January (3 odd days), February (0), March (3), April (2). Total odd days from Jan 1 = 8 ≡ 1. Since Jan 1 was Friday, May 1 was Saturday. A 31-day month starting on Saturday has 4 Fridays (7th, 14th, 21st, 28th).

Hence, **January** is the month that had 5 Fridays.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **Alternate Method__**

Using the day determination formula for **January 1, 1926**:

Day = (Date + Month Code + Century Code + Year + Leap Year Code) mod 7

 
• Date = 1
 
• Month Code (January, ordinary year) = 0
 
• Century Code (1900s) = 0
 
• Year = 26
 
• Leap Year Code (26 ÷ 4) = 6

Total = (1 + 0 + 0 + 26 + 6) = 33

33 ÷ 7 = 4 weeks and a remainder of 5.

In the day code system (0=Sun, 1=Mon, 2=Tue, 3=Wed, 4=Thu, 5=Fri, 6=Sat), the remainder 5 represents **Friday**.

Since **January 1** is a Friday and the month has 31 days, it contains 5 Fridays.

Hence, the correct answer is **January**.

questions.question: At what time (approximately) (in AM) between 5 AM and 6 AM will the angle between the hour and the minute hand of a clock be 135 degrees?
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

Hour hand covers 3600 in 12 hours

Angular distance covered in 1 hour = 360/12 = 300

Angular distance covered in 60 minutes = 300

Angular distance covered in 1 minute = 1/20

__Calculation:__

Minute hand covers 360 in 60 minutes

1 minute = 360/60 ⇒ 1 minute = 60

The time is between **5 AM** and **6 AM**. Let the required time be 5 hours and **M** minutes.

Angle covered by the **minute hand** in M minutes = M × 60 = 6M0

Angle covered by the **hour hand** in 5 hours and M minutes = 5 × 30 + M × ½ = 150 + M/2

According to the question, the angle between the hands is **135 degrees**.

|(150 + M/2) − 6M| = 135

|150 − 5.5M| = 135

**Case 1:**

150 − 5.5M = 135

5.5M = 15

M = 15/5.5 = 150/55 = 30/11 ≈ 2.727 minutes

Rounding to the nearest minute, **M ≈ 3**.

**Case 2:**

150 − 5.5M = −135

5.5M = 150 + 135 = 285

M = 285/5.5 = 2850/55 = 570/11 ≈ 51.818 minutes

Rounding to the nearest minute, **M ≈ 52**.

Comparing with the given options, the approximate time is **5:03**.

Hence, the angle between the hour and minute hands is 135 degrees at **5:03**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

The angle between the **hour hand** and **minute hand** = |60H - 11M| over 2

Here, **H = 5** and **Angle = 135**.

135 = |60 times 5 - 11 times M| over 2

270 = |300 − 11M|

300 − 11M = 270 OR 300 − 11M = −270

11M = 30 OR 11M = 570

M = 30/11 ≈ 2.72 OR M = 570/11 ≈ 51.81

The approximate value from the options is **M = 3**.

Therefore, the time is **5:03**.

Hence, the correct answer is **5:03**.

questions.question: At what time (approximately) (in AM) between 8 AM and 9 AM will the hour and minute hands of the clock overlap?
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

The **hour hand** covers 360° in 12 hours.

Angular distance covered by the hour hand in 1 hour = 360/12 = 30°

Angular distance covered by the hour hand in 1 minute = 30/60 = 1/2° per minute.

The **minute hand** covers 360° in 60 minutes.

Angular distance covered by the minute hand in 1 minute = 360/60 = 6° per minute.

When the **hour and minute hands** overlap, the angle between them is 0°.

__Calculation:__

The time is between **8 AM** and **9 AM**, so H = 8.

Let the hands overlap at **M** minutes past 8.

Angle covered by the **hour hand** from 12 o'clock = 8 × 30 + M × 1/2 = 240 + M/2

Angle covered by the **minute hand** from 12 o'clock = M × 6 = 6M

Since the hands **overlap**, these angles must be equal:

6M = 240 + M/2

6M − M/2 = 240

11M/2 = 240

11M = 480

M = 480/11 = 43.6363...

Rounding to the nearest whole number, M ≈ 44 minutes.

Therefore, the hands will overlap at approximately **8:44 AM**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

The formula for the angle between the hands is: Angle = |30H − (11/2)M|

For the hands to overlap, Angle = 0.

0 = |30 × 8 − (11/2)M|

0 = 240 − 5.5M

5.5M = 240

M = 240/5.5 = 480/11

M = 43.6363... minutes ≈ 44 minutes.

Hence, the correct answer is **8:44**.

questions.question: The ratio of present ages of two students is 10 : 13. The difference between their ages is 9 years. 6 years ago from present, what was the ratio of the ages of these two students?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Present age ratio = 10 : 13

Difference in ages = 9 years

**Calculation:**

Difference in ratio = 13 − 10 = 3 parts

3 parts = 9 years

1 part = 9 ÷ 3 = 3 years

Present ages:

10 × 3 = 30 years

13 × 3 = 39 years

**6 years ago:**

30 − 6 = 24 years

39 − 6 = 33 years

Required ratio = 24 : 33 = 8 : 11

Hence, the correct answer is** "Option 3".**

questions.question: Which mountain pass connects Ladakh with Kashmir Valley?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Zoji La**__.

__
 
• **Zoji La** is a high-altitude mountain pass located in the **Himalayan Range** within the Union Territory of **Ladakh**, India.
 
• It serves as the vital geographical link between the **Kashmir Valley** (specifically near **Sonamarg**) and the **Ladakh** region, providing access to **Drass**, **Kargil**, and **Leh**.
 
• The pass is situated at an approximate elevation of **3,528 meters** (**11,575 feet**) above sea level, making it one of the most dangerous and strategically important passes in the world.
 
• It is a critical component of **National Highway 1** (NH 1), which facilitates the movement of supplies and military personnel between **Srinagar** and **Leh**.
 
• Due to extreme weather conditions and heavy snowfall, the pass remains closed for nearly six months every year, leading to the development of the **Zojila Tunnel** to provide year-round connectivity.

questions.question: Xuanzang's account is particularly valuable for the study of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Harshavardhana's court**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Xuanzang**, a prominent **Chinese Buddhist monk** and traveler, visited India during the **7th Century CE** (specifically between **629–645 CE**) during the reign of **King Harshavardhana**.
 
• His famous travelogue, **Si-Yu-Ki** (Record of the Western World), provides a comprehensive eye-witness account of the **political, social, and economic conditions** of the **Vardhana Empire**.
 
• He spent several years at **Harshavardhana's court** and at **Nalanda University**, where he studied under the guidance of the monk **Shilabhadra**, documenting the high standards of education and religious debates of that era.
 
• The monk vividly describes the **Kannauj Assembly** and the **Prayag Assembly**, highlighting Harsha's religious tolerance and his massive patronage of **Mahayana Buddhism** and public welfare.
 
• Xuanzang’s records are essential for understanding the transition from the ancient to the early medieval period in India, particularly regarding the **administration** and the city of **Kannauj**, which served as the imperial capital.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Comparison with other historical periods mentioned in the options:
 
 
• **Harappan towns**: This **Indus Valley Civilization** flourished during the **Bronze Age** (c. 3300–1300 BCE); knowledge of this period is based entirely on **archaeological excavations** at sites like **Mohenjo-daro** and **Harappa**.
 
• **Mauryan polity**: This era (c. 322–185 BCE) is primarily studied through **Kautilya’s Arthashastra**, the **Indica** by the Greek ambassador **Megasthenes**, and the **Edicts of Ashoka**.
 
• **Chola naval expeditions**: These were prominent during the **10th and 11th Centuries CE** under rulers like **Rajaraja I** and **Rajendra Chola I**; they are documented in **Tamil inscriptions** and copper plates, long after Xuanzang's return to China.

• The **Charter Act of 1813**, also known as the **East India Company Act 1813**, was enacted by the **British Parliament** to renew the **East India Company's (EIC)** charter for another **20 years**.
 
• A landmark provision of this Act was the **abolition of the trade monopoly** of the Company in **India**, effectively opening **Indian trade** to all **British merchants** and private traders.
 
• Despite the liberalization of general trade, the **East India Company** retained its **exclusive monopoly** over the **tea trade** and all commercial **trade with China**.
 
• The shift toward **Free Trade** was largely influenced by the **Napoleonic Wars** and the **Continental System**, which restricted British access to **European markets** and forced the search for new economic avenues in **Asia**.
 
• The Act was significant for formally asserting the **sovereignty of the British Crown** over the territories held by the Company in **India**.

• It mandated the Company to set aside a sum of **1 lakh rupees** annually for the **promotion of education**, literature, and the **knowledge of sciences** among the inhabitants of British India.
 
 
 
• **Transition to 1833**:
 
 
• The **Charter Act of 1833** later removed the remaining **monopolies on tea** and **trade with China**, transforming the **East India Company** into a purely **administrative and political body**.
 
• It also led to the centralization of administration, making the **Governor-General of Bengal** the **Governor-General of India**.

• The **melting point** is the temperature at which a substance changes its state from **solid to liquid** at standard atmospheric pressure.
 
• On the **Celsius scale**, the melting point of pure ice is defined as **0°C** under a standard pressure of **1 atmosphere** (1 atm).
 
• The **Kelvin scale** is the **SI unit** of temperature, and the conversion between Celsius and Kelvin is given by the formula: **T(K) = t(°C) + 273.15**.
 
• By applying this relationship, the melting point of ice in Kelvin is calculated as **0 + 273.15 = 273.15 K**.
 
• Unlike the Celsius or Fahrenheit scales, the Kelvin scale is an **absolute scale** and does not use the degree symbol.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **373.15**:

 
 
• This value represents the **boiling point of water** on the Kelvin scale.
 
• It corresponds to **100°C** on the Celsius scale (100 + 273.15 = 373.15 K).
 
 
 
• **0**:
 
 
• On the Kelvin scale, **0 K** is known as **Absolute Zero**, the temperature at which all thermal motion of particles ceases.
 
• In Celsius, Absolute Zero is equivalent to **−273.15°C**.
 
 
 
• **100**:
 
 
• This is the numerical value for the **boiling point of water** in degrees **Celsius**.
 
• It marks the transition from the liquid phase to the gaseous phase at sea level.
 
 
 
• **Triple Point of Water**:
 
 
• Water can coexist in all three states (solid, liquid, and gas) at a specific temperature of **273.16 K** (0.01°C) and a partial vapor pressure of **611.657 Pascals**.

questions.question: The Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction agreement is an international treaty under the ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**UNCLOS**__.

__
 
• The **Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ)** agreement, commonly referred to as the **High Seas Treaty**, is an international legally binding instrument established under the framework of the **United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS)**.
 
• Its primary objective is the **conservation** and **sustainable use** of marine biological diversity in areas that lie beyond the **Exclusive Economic Zones (EEZ)** and continental shelves of coastal states, which encompass approximately **64 percent** of the ocean surface.
 
• The treaty was officially adopted on **June 19, 2023**, after nearly **20 years** of discussions and negotiations to address legal gaps in **global ocean governance**.
 
• It operates on four key pillars: the **sharing of benefits** from **Marine Genetic Resources (MGRs)**; the use of **Area-Based Management Tools (ABMTs)**, including **Marine Protected Areas (MPAs)**; the conduct of **Environmental Impact Assessments (EIAs)** for deep-sea activities; and **Capacity Building and the Transfer of Marine Technology (CBTMT)** to assist developing nations.
 
• The **BBNJ** is considered the **third implementing agreement** under **UNCLOS**, following the **1994 Part XI Agreement** and the **1995 Fish Stocks Agreement**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **UNCLOS (United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea)**:

 
 
• Adopted in **1982** and effective from **1994**, it is often called the **Constitution of the Oceans**.
 
• It defines the **legal status** of various maritime zones, including **Territorial Seas** (up to **12 nautical miles**) and **EEZs** (up to **200 nautical miles**).
 
 
 
• **UNESCO (United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization)**:
 
 
• While it hosts the **Intergovernmental Oceanographic Commission (IOC)**, which provides scientific data for the **BBNJ**, it is not the governing body for this specific treaty.
 
 
 
• **WTO (World Trade Organization)**:
 
 
• An organization focused on **global trade rules** and dispute resolution; it does not possess jurisdiction over **maritime biological conservation**.

questions.question: The average of 110 numbers is 70.5. By addition of 40 new numbers, the average becomes 55.1. What is the sum of newly added numbers?

Identify the **net deviation** from the initial average: 55.1 − 70.5 = −15.4.

The total decrease for 110 numbers is 110 × (−15.4) = −1694.

Sum of 40 new numbers = (New count × New average) − (Old count × Old average).

Sum = (40 × 55.1) + (Net decrease from old group) = 2204 − 1694 = 510.

**∴ The correct answer is 510.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Initial average (A₁) = 70.5

Number of added numbers (n₂) = 40

Total numbers (N) = 110 + 40 = 150

Final average (Aₜₒₜₐₗ) = 55.1

**Formula Used:**

Sum = **Average** × **Total Numbers**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/88287342cd494dfbc0aedd1cf6e86119d8fb4da1f38c6268dc4dbdf5e29e05eb.png]

⇒ Total sum of 110 numbers = 110 × 70.5 = 7755

⇒ Total sum of 150 numbers = 150 × 55.1 = 8265

⇒ Sum of 40 newly added numbers = Total sum (150) − Initial sum (110)

⇒ Sum = 8265 − 7755

⇒ Sum = 510

**∴ The correct answer is 510.**

questions.question: A is smallest 3 digit number divisible by both 14 and 20. B is the largest 3 digit number divisible by 14 and 20. What is the value of B - A?

Difference **B − A** = 980 − 140 = 840.

**∴ The correct answer is 840.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Numbers are 14 and 20. **A** is the smallest 3-digit common multiple. **B** is the largest 3-digit common multiple.

**Formula Used:** LCM(x, y) gives the smallest common multiple. All other common multiples are multiples of the **LCM**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/db2819780a498384f55e16c6067a06e8c6a230ad5e295934db0161351f1e6f56.png] 

⇒ Prime factorization: 14 = 2 × 7 and 20 = 2² × 5.

⇒ **LCM**(14, 20) = 2² × 5 × 7 = 4 × 5 × 7 = 140.

⇒ Smallest 3-digit multiple (**A**) = 140 × 1 = 140.

⇒ To find **B**, divide 999 by 140: 999 ÷ 140 ≈ 7.13.

⇒ Largest 3-digit multiple (**B**) = 140 × 7 = 980.

⇒ Value of **B − A** = 980 − 140 = 840.

**∴ The correct answer is 840.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM (Least Common Multiple)

The smallest positive integer that is perfectly divisible by two or more numbers. Common multiples of numbers are always multiples of their **LCM**.

HCF and LCM Relation

For any two numbers x and y, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their **HCF** and **LCM**: x × y = HCF(x,y) × LCM(x,y).

Finding Multiples in a Range

To find the number of multiples of k between m and n, calculate the difference between ⌊n/k⌋ and ⌊(m−1)/k⌋.

questions.question: An article is sold for a loss Rs. 69. Loss percentage is 30 percent. What is the selling price of the article?

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 161.**

questions.question: A train crosses a standing pole in 25 seconds and a platform of length 500 metre in 75 seconds. What is the speed (in m/s) of train?

Extra distance = **Length of platform** = 500 m.

**Speed of train** = Distance ÷ Time = 500 ÷ 50 = 10 m/s.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 m/s.**

Time to cross **pole** (T₁) = 25 s

⇒ S = L ÷ 25 — (Equation 1)

When crossing a **platform**, distance = L + 500.

⇒ S = (L + 500) ÷ 75 — (Equation 2)

Equating Equation 1 and Equation 2:

⇒ L ÷ 25 = (L + 500) ÷ 75

⇒ 3 × L = L + 500

⇒ 2L = 500

⇒ L = 250 m

Now, calculate speed using Equation 1:

⇒ Speed = 250 ÷ 25

⇒ Speed = 10 m/s

**∴ The correct answer is 10 m/s.**

When two objects move in the **same direction**, relative speed = S₁ − S₂. In **opposite directions**, relative speed = S₁ + S₂.

• To convert a **Past Perfect** sentence into **Passive Voice**, the standard grammatical formula is: **New Subject (Object of Active)** + **had** + **been** + **Past Participle (V3)** + **by + New Object (Subject of Active)**.

• The **Object** of the active sentence, **eight suspects**, becomes the **Subject** of the passive sentence as it is the entity receiving the action.

• The **auxiliary verb** **been** must be inserted between **had** and the main verb **rounded up** to correctly denote the **Passive** state of the **Perfect Tense**.

• The **agent**, **by the police**, identifies the performer of the action, and the **adverbial phrase** of time, **before the press conference**, remains at the end to provide the necessary temporal context.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Grammatical Variations and Errors**:

• **Simple Past Passive**: This uses **were + V3** (e.g., **were rounded up**). While grammatically correct in isolation, it fails to preserve the **Past-in-the-Past** relationship established by the original **had**.

• **Morphological Accuracy**: The word **being** is used for **Continuous Tenses**. Combining **had** with **being** (as in **had being rounded up**) results in a **Morphological Error** as it violates the rules of English **auxiliary verb** sequencing.

• **Semantic Shift**: Maintaining the **Active Voice** but swapping the **Subject** and **Object** (e.g., **suspects had rounded up the police**) causes a **Semantic Shift**, reversing the meaning of the original statement.

• **Past Perfect Utility**: This tense is specifically used to show that an action (the arrest) was completed before another event in the past (the press conference).

</ul

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into active voice?

Will the necessary arrangements be made by the volunteers before the guests reach the venue?

options.text: Do the volunteers make the necessary arrangements before the guests reach the venue?
Did the volunteers make the necessary arrangements before the guests reach the venue?
Will the volunteers make the necessary arrangements before the guests reach the venue?
Have the volunteers made the necessary arrangements before the guests reach the venue?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Will the volunteers make the necessary arrangements before the guests reach the venue?**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence is in the **Passive Voice** of the **Simple Future Tense** in an **interrogative form**. The structure is: **Will/Shall + Object + be + V3 (Past Participle) + by + Subject?**
 
• To convert this into the **Active Voice**, the **agent** of the action (**the volunteers**) must become the subject of the sentence, and the **receiver** of the action (**the necessary arrangements**) must become the object.
 
• The conversion rule for the **Simple Future Active Voice** (Interrogative) is: **Will/Shall + Subject + V1 (Base Form) + Object?**
 
• The auxiliary **be** is omitted in the active voice, and the past participle **made** is converted to its base form **make**.
 
• The secondary clause **before the guests reach the venue** is already in the active voice and serves as a temporal modifier; thus, it remains unchanged in the final conversion.
 
• Applying these steps, **the volunteers** (subject) performs the action **make** (verb) on **the necessary arrangements** (object), resulting in the correct active construction.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Simple Future Tense Structure**:
 
 
• **Active**: **Subject + will/shall + V1 + Object**.
 
• **Passive**: **Object + will/shall + be + V3 + by + Subject**.
 
 
 
• **Identifying Incorrect Tense Conversions**:
 
 
• **Simple Present**: Uses **Do/Does** as seen in Option 1. This is incorrect because the original sentence refers to a future intent.
 
• **Simple Past**: Uses **Did** as seen in Option 2. This is incorrect because it implies the action was already completed in the past.
 
• **Present Perfect**: Uses **Has/Have + V3** as seen in Option 4. This is incorrect as it describes a completed action with present relevance, rather than a future one.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into active voice?
The secret documents are guarded by someone day and night.

options.text: Someone guards the secret documents day and night.
Someone has guarded the secret documents day and night.
Someone is guarding the secret documents day and night.
Someone was guarding the secret documents day and night.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Someone guards the secret documents day and night**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The original sentence is in the **Passive Voice** using the **Simple Present Tense**, identifiable by the construction **is/am/are + V3 (past participle)**.

• When converting from passive to active voice, the **agent** or performer of the action (found after the preposition **by**) becomes the **subject** of the active sentence. Here, **someone** becomes the new subject.

• The **subject** of the passive sentence (the secret documents) shifts to the **object** position in the active voice sentence.

• The verb **are guarded** must be changed to the active form of the **Simple Present Tense**. Since **someone** is an **indefinite pronoun** and is treated as **singular**, the base verb **guard** takes the **-s** suffix to become **guards**.

• The time-related phrase **day and night** is an **adverbial adjunct** and remains at the end of the sentence to maintain the original context and meaning.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Tense Variations in Active Voice**:

• **Present Perfect Tense**: Used in option 2 (**has guarded**), this tense indicates an action that happened at an unspecified time in the past or has recently concluded. The passive form would be **have been guarded**.

• **Present Continuous Tense**: Used in option 3 (**is guarding**), this indicates an action currently in progress. The passive form would require the addition of **being** (e.g., **are being guarded**).

• **Past Continuous Tense**: Used in option 4 (**was guarding**), this describes an action that was ongoing at a specific point in the past. Its passive equivalent would be **were being guarded**.

• **Active vs. Passive Voice Rules**:

• In **Active Voice**, the subject performs the action (e.g., **Subject + Verb + Object**).

• In **Passive Voice**, the subject receives the action (e.g., **Object + be verb + V3 + by + Subject**).

• The **tense** must never change when converting between voices; only the **structure** and **emphasis** are altered.

</ul

questions.question:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions based on the passage:

Why did Einstein suggest using a movable slit in his version of the double-slit experiment?

options.text: To eliminate interference patterns completely and analyse their result
To measure the photon's momentum and determine its path
To increase the number of photons passing through the slits
To reduce uncertain behaviour in the photon's position

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the passage, **Albert Einstein** proposed a variation of the **double-slit experiment** in the **1920s** involving a **movable slit**.
 
• The purpose of this light, movable slit was that it would **recoil** when a **single photon** passed through it.
 
• By measuring that **recoil** (which involves the transfer of **momentum**), one could theoretically **determine the path** the photon took (which slit it passed through).
 
• Einstein's objective was to see if one could simultaneously obtain **path information** and observe an **interference pattern**, potentially highlighting a conflict within **quantum theory**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **To measure the photon's momentum and determine its path**.

 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Niels Bohr** countered Einstein's idea by arguing that the **uncertainty principle** would prevent such a measurement from working without destroying the **interference pattern**.
 
• Modern researchers have recently successfully tested this idea by replacing the movable slit with a **single atom** cooled to its **ground state**.
 
• The **interference pattern** is a classic indicator that light (or matter) is behaving like a **wave**, while knowing the specific **path** suggests **particle-like** behavior.
</ul

questions.question:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions based on the passage:

What principle of quantum mechanics did Bohr rely on to argue against Einstein's proposal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the passage, **Niels Bohr** argued against **Albert Einstein's** proposal by relying on the **uncertainty principle**.
 
• Einstein suggested that measuring the **recoil** of a movable slit could determine the **path** of a photon (particle behavior) while still observing an **interference pattern** (wave behavior).
 
• Bohr countered that any measurement precise enough to determine the **recoil momentum** would, according to the **uncertainty principle**, create a corresponding uncertainty in the slit's **position**.
 
• This uncertainty in position would be large enough to destroy the **interference pattern**, thereby upholding the laws of **quantum mechanics**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **1**.

 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **The Principle of Superposition**: States that a quantum system can exist in **multiple states** simultaneously until a measurement is made.
 
• **The Principle of Complementarity**: A broader philosophical framework by Bohr stating that **wave and particle** aspects are complementary but mutually exclusive in a single experiment.
 
• **The Exclusion Principle**: Proposed by **Wolfgang Pauli**, it states that no two **fermions** (like electrons) can occupy the same quantum state within a system.
</ul

Why is it important in modern experiments to cool the atom as close as possible to its ground state?

options.text: To eliminate all motion so that data measurement is easier
To ensure that the atom consistently emits photons.
To prevent any interaction between the atom and the laser beam.
To reduce random motions within the constraints of quantum limits.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage explicitly mentions that researchers **cooled the atom close to its ground state** to ensure its **random motion** was as small as **quantum physics** allowed.
 
• In this ground state, the **uncertainty in the atom's momentum** becomes comparable to the **momentum of a single photon**.
 
• This level of cooling is necessary because if the atom had high **thermal or random motion**, it would be impossible to detect the tiny **recoil** caused by a single photon passing through.
 
• Therefore, the primary goal is **to reduce random motions** so they stay within the fundamental **constraints of quantum limits**, making the experiment viable.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1** is incorrect because according to the **Uncertainty Principle**, it is impossible to eliminate *all* motion; there is always a minimum zero-point energy.
 
• **Option 2** is incorrect because the cooling is for **momentum/recoil sensitivity**, not specifically to regulate the rate of photon emission.
 
• **Option 3** is incorrect because the **laser beam** is the tool used to trap and hold the atom in place; preventing interaction would stop the experiment from working.
 
• **Ground State:** This refers to the lowest energy state of a quantum mechanical system, where **quantum fluctuations** are the only remaining source of motion.
</ul

What does this experiment set out to test about the relationship between path information and interference?

options.text: Whether or not photons purely behave as particles
Interference can take place without slits.
Whether knowing the path of the photon takes away interference
Whether atoms can replace photons in interference experiments

questions.solution:

__

• Einstein's goal was to determine if one could simultaneously measure the **recoil** of a slit (to identify the **photon's path**) and observe an **interference pattern**.
 
• Researchers from the **University of Science and Technology of China** used a **single atom** to act as a movable slit to test this relationship.
 
• The study specifically investigated how obtaining **which-way information** (via the **atom's recoil**) influences the presence or visibility of the **interference pattern**, which is a hallmark of wave behavior.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Summary of Experiment Goal:** *"The researchers aimed to check whether the **atom's recoil** could be used to say which way a **photon** went and how that **path information affected the interference pattern**."*

 

**Additional Information__**

questions.question:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions based on the passage:

Why is the uncertainty in the atom's momentum significant in this experiment?

options.text: It determines the wavelength of the photon
It keeps the atom stationary during the experiment.
It permits the photon to go through both slits simultaneously
It limits the precision of recoil measurement.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **It limits the precision of recoil measurement.**

 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the modern version of **Einstein's** experiment, a **single atom** is used to act as the **movable slit**.
 
• The researchers cooled the atom to its **ground state**, ensuring its **random motion** reached the minimum allowed by **quantum physics**.
 
• The passage notes that in this state, the **uncertainty in the atom's momentum** is similar to the **momentum of a single photon**.
 
• This **uncertainty** is critical because it represents a fundamental limit; if the uncertainty of the atom's inherent momentum is high, it masks the small change in momentum (the **recoil**) caused by the photon.
 
• Therefore, this uncertainty directly **limits the precision** with which the **recoil measurement** can be made to determine the **photon's path**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **It limits the precision of recoil measurement.**

 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **The Uncertainty Principle:** Proposed by **Werner Heisenberg**, it states that the more precisely the **position** of a particle is known, the less precisely its **momentum** can be known, and vice versa.
 
• **Niels Bohr** argued that **Einstein's** plan would fail because the act of measuring the **recoil momentum** would create a corresponding uncertainty in the **slit's position**, which would then wash out the **interference pattern**.
 
• **Wave-Particle Duality:** This experiment explores the fundamental quantum concept that light can exhibit both **wave-like** (interference) and **particle-like** (recoil/path) properties, but typically not both simultaneously with full clarity.
</ul
